correctness.rationale: Conditioning on the beta denominator gives an exact one-dimensional survival integral. A single substitution reduces it to a small-lower-limit integral whose behavior changes at q=2. The three regimes follow from elementary integration by parts and local expansion of 1-exp(-t). The moment cutoff follows independently from the product representation and the exact inverse-Rayleigh and beta inverse moments. The standalone checker verifies the exact formulas numerically but is not used as proof.

value.rationale: Tail flexibility is an explicit motivation of the SIR construction and of its application to data with large observations. The exact phase theorem shows that q controls the power-law index only below 2, while the inverse-Rayleigh parent caps that index thereafter. The critical logarithm at q=2 is a natural boundary phenomenon, and the same classification immediately settles every positive real moment and the terminal hazard. This materially sharpens interpretation of q, including simulation and regression regimes with q at or above 2.
